entry.title: Keep the choices easy to see
entry.summary: Set out a few complete activities your child is interested in, with their pieces together and a familiar place to return them.
entry.cue: Notice what gets used, what is too difficult, and what has stopped inviting another turn.
detail: A basket or tray can show what belongs together. Davies sets out a puzzle undone and keeps needed pieces available; an incomplete activity can be put aside until its missing piece is found.
Store unused or currently difficult activities for another time, and rotate when your child is looking for a new challenge. The book does not ask for a fixed number or a rotation schedule.
Show where things belong and share putting them back. If your child is already absorbed in the next activity, Davies sometimes models the return herself.

displayContext.footer: You don’t need a different home. Start with what you have.
displayContext.colophon: Original summaries inspired by The Montessori Baby and The Montessori Toddler. Open any idea for its book references. The illustration is an invitation to explore, rather than a room to reproduce. Follow your child’s pace.
